newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Oct private sector credit growth 14.3pct y/y.
newsitem.headline: Irish Oct private sector credit growth 14.3pct y/y.

text.p: The adjusted annual rate of growth of Irish private-sector credit grew to 14.3 percent in October from 13.3 percent at end-September, central bank monthly statistics showed on Thursday.
The annual rate of increase in residential mortgage lending by all credit institutions rose to 17.1 percent from 16.5 percent, the bank said.
The adjusted rate of broad money-supply growth (M3E) fell to 12.4 percent from 12.8 percent, the central bank said.

It said the annual rate M3E growth fluctuated within a range of around 12 to 13 percent for six consecutive months up to end-October and private sector credit growth also remained strong, averaging around 14 percent in recent months.
"The rate of growth in total domestic credit has been somewhat slower since government credit contracted significantly in the six months to end-October, the central bank said.

It said the greater part of the increase in private-sector credit in October was Irish pound denominated, although the foreign-currency component was larger than in recent months growing by 225 million Irish pounds, of which only 32 million was IFSC-related.
Private sector credit grew by 559 million Irish pounds in October, the biggest monthly increase since March.
Mortgage lending accounted for almost half of the 334 million increase in Irish-pound credit.
Residential mortgages rose by 126 million and other mortgages rose by 41 million.
Non-mortgage Irish pound credit increased at an annual rate of 14.2 percent in October, unchanged from the previous month.
Irish pound overdrafts fell by 93 million but loans up to and including one year rose by 20 million while term and revolving loans rose by 131 million.
